rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (score 701.3, best so far): the oval (20/20, 1.82 s, max_error 0.012 m) and s-bend (20/20, steering_oscillation 0.29) now finish reliably. The slalom still fails 20/20 with progress 0.47 and about 1.05 line-loss events per run. The kd sweep on the slalom gave 0.23 (kd 0.8), 0.42 (kd 1.1), 0.47 (kd 1.5), so the gains are diminishing. Earlier geometry changes (wider array, forward sensors, higher kp) all hurt, so geometry stays fixed. Changes: kd 1.5 to 1.8 to add damping at sharp left-right alternations, and base_speed 1.0 to 0.95 to give the loop more time to correct on the slalom. The s-bend has margin (20/20, progress 0.997), so a small speed cut should cost little there and only a few tenths of a second on the oval. Hypotheses: H1, the slalom is still limited by lag at alternations, so kd 1.8 pushes progress toward 0.55 or more. H2, the speed cut lowers the lateral excursions that cause line loss, so line_loss_events fall below about 0.8. H3 (risk), kd 1.8 amplifies sensor noise, so steering_oscillation on the s-bend rises above about 0.4 and noise_robustness drops. If that happens, kd should return to about 1.4 and the next test is sensor_size 0.012. Expected result: slalom progress 0.55 or more, s-bend still 18/20 or better, oval completion_time about 1.85 s. Next measurements: slalom progress and line_loss_events, s-bend completion and off-track count, steering_oscillation and max_error on all tracks, and noise_robustness to check whether noise is becoming the limit.
